title: The Valley That Kept Filling Up
story: Glendrossel has gnawed a mud dam across the river mouth, and the stilt-village of Reedhollow is slowly drowning: the water rises 0.8 feet every hour. Mr 6 cranks open an old sluice gate that drains 0.3 feet every hour, which helps — but not enough. The water stands at 4.4 feet, and the villagers' stilt floors flood at 12 feet.
question: How many hours do the villagers have before the water reaches 12 feet?
solution: With the sluice open, the water really rises 0.8 − 0.3 = 0.5 feet each hour.
The water still has 12 − 4.4 = 7.6 feet to climb.
praise: Working with the rise-per-hour was smart thinking — the step that was missing was subtracting the sluice's drain to get the real rate.
hint: The water climbs and drains at the same time — what is the true rise each hour once the sluice is open?
victory: Mr 6 uses every one of those 15.2 hours to walk the village to high ground, and Glendrossel, finding nothing left to flood, sheepishly gnaws his own dam back open.
imagePrompt: A huge shaggy river beast with chisel teeth perched on a mud dam above a half-flooded village of stilt houses, while a small numeral-6 knight hauls open a rusted sluice gate in grey rainy light.
